content.title: National champions! Michigan powers past UConn to finish off historic season
content.text: INDIANAPOLIS — Michigan, undoubtedly, is now the best team in college basketball. The Wolverines beat UConn 69-63 on Monday night to claim their second national championship.Michigan’s only other national championship trophy, from 1989, has company. The Wolverines became the first Big Ten team to win it all since 2000 when Michigan State did. A Big Ten women’s team, UCLA, ended a title drought Sunday that was a year longer. Dusty May became a champion in just his second season as head coach.The Wolverines played far from their best offensively, shooting 2 for 15 from deep, and still prevailed. They made 25 of 28 free throws (89%), one of their best games from the line. Elliot Cadeau scored 19 and Morez Johnson Jr. added 12 points and 10 rebounds for the victors. Yaxel Lendeborg, who hurt his left leg in a Final Four blowout against Arizona, did not look like himself and scored 13.Cadeau was named the Most Outstanding Player of the Final Four.Michigan led by four at halftime, pushed the lead to 11 with 12:56 left, and didn’t let UConn, which won it all in 2023 and 2023, get closer than four for the entire second half. Trey McKenney’s 3 appeared the be the dagger, giving Michigan a nine-point lead and causing Dan Hurley to take a timeout with 1:49 left. The Huskies, though, had one last push.UConn’s steal and banked 3 cut the margin to four and Michigan’s Roddy Gayle Jr. missed a pair of free throws with 29 seconds left. Alex Karaban’s 3 at the other end grazed the rim. McKenney made two free throws with 13 seconds left, UConn’s final shot missed, and Aday Mara stuffed the game ball under his jersey as maize and blue confetti rained on the Lucas Oil Stadium court.Michigan, the No. 1 seed from the Midwest Region, finished 37-3 and in a tie with Illinois for the most wins by a Big Ten team in a season.Karaban led UConn in scoring with 17. Tarris Reed Jr., a former Wolverine, scored 13 points and had 14 rebounds. The Huskies shot under 31% from the field.Michigan did enough down the stretch to win it all. Cadeau somehow powered through a foul, Solo Ball’s fourth, for a basket and made the free throw to give Michigan a 38-31 lead with 16:20 left. Lendeborg scored through a foul to push the margin to eight a minute later.Cadeau scored twice, including Michigan’s first 3 in 11 tries, to make it 48-37 with 12:56 left. UConn didn’t wilt and cut the margin to five with 8:24 left before a lob to Mara gave Michigan some breathing room.Michigan led 7-2 but didn’t have good rhythm offensively. Alex Karaban’s second 3 gave UConn its first lead, 16-13, with 10:23 left. Lendeborg didn’t make his presence known until after that, missing a couple of shots. The game went back and forth for a stretch, with the slow pace favoring UConn. Cadeau picked up his second foul with 6:24 left in the first half and went to the bench, not returning until final possession before the break.Karaban was called for a hook-and-hold with 3:16 left on Johnson. He made both free throws to tie the game and Mara found Lendeborg underneath for a basket, the start of a 6-0 run that gave Michigan a 29-25 lead. Gayle’s incredible putback dunk on a fast break had Lendeborg in awe. Michigan missed all eight 3s, the first time all season it hadn’t made a 3 in a half, but still led 33-29 at half.The shots weren’t splashing in the second half but Michigan won anyway. UConn finished 9 for 33 from deep and overall had its worst shooting performance of the season.Saturday’s Final Four was billed as a heavyweight showdown and Michigan knocked out Arizona in the first round. The Wolverines led by 30 midway through the second half and won 91-73.Michigan had scored at least 90 points the past five games, setting an NCAA Tournament record for consecutive games with at least that many, but came up well shot of the number Monday. Michigan is 8-1 in national semifinal games and for just the second time was able to win the next game.UConn (34-6) beat Illinois on Saturday 71-62 to reach the final game. The Huskies were 22-1 at one point and, like Michigan, did not win their conference tournament. They beat Furman and UCLA comfortably in Philadelphia before escaping Michigan State and Duke to reach the Final Four. Braylon Mullins’ deep 3 just before the buzzer gave UConn a one-point win over Duke. Michigan won the Big Ten Tournament and reached the Sweet 16 last season, May’s first. The Wolverines eyed a much bigger prize this season. By the time they won the Big Ten regular-season title by four games, they knew they had a chance.Lendeborg played his last game in college and will be a first-round NBA draft pick. Mara and Johnson have eligibility but decisions to make about the NBA. Nimari Burnett, Roddy Gayle Jr., and Will Tschetter are out of eligibility. It will be another rebuild for May, though how much of one remains to be seen. Transfers and coaching changes typically happen; assistant coach Justin Joyner has already accepted the head job at Oregon State.Michigan started 13-0 with an average victory margin of more than 30 points; all but three were decided by at least 25 points. The run included an unprecedented performance in Las Vegas, where Michigan ripped through the Players Era Championship, winning three games in three days by a combined 110 points. That’s when Michigan established itself a national force.Even if the Wolverines’ single-digit Big Ten wins were turned to losses, they still would have won the league. They entered the Big Ten Tournament with two losses, a surprise home setback to Wisconsin by three and a neutral-court loss to Duke by five. Even with a loss to Purdue in the conference tournament final by eight, they entered the Big Dance as a No. 1 seed.The Wolverines didn’t have to travel far the postseason. They played in Chicago for the Big Ten Tournament and Buffalo, New York, to start the NCAA Tournament, beating Howard and Saint Louis. They returned to Chicago and a pair of SEC teams, Alabama and Tennessee, to reach Indianapolis.Once there, they finished the job.👉 The Ann Arbor News commemorated Michigan’s national championship with a collectible front page — available here: https://newskeepsake.com/pages/ann-arbor‘We shocked the world.
